name: Slack
summary: Slack uses a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization‑code flow (v2) with bot and optional user scopes. First create a Slack app, configure redirect URLs and scopes, then generate an install link and exchange the code for an access token.

oauth_note.text: OAuth 2.0 authorization‑code flow (v2). Supports bot scopes via scope= and optional user scopes via user_scope=. No PKCE support mentioned.

app_types.name: Slack App (OAuth)
app_types.when_to_use: When you need a bot or user token to call Slack APIs

registration_access_claim.text: Anyone with a Slack account and a workspace they are a member of can create an app; a free workspace created minutes earlier was enough.

prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace and a logged‑in Slack account to access the developer portal
Client ID and Client Secret from the app’s Basic Information page

steps.title: Create a new Slack app
steps.detail: Log into https://api.slack.com/apps, click “Create New App”, choose a name and workspace, and confirm.

steps.title: Add OAuth redirect URL(s)
steps.detail: In the app’s OAuth & Permissions page, add your HTTPS redirect URI (e.g., https://yourdomain.com/slack/callback).

steps.title: Select required scopes
steps.detail: Add bot scopes under “Scopes” (e.g., incoming-webhook) and optional user scopes under “User Token Scopes”. Each distinct set of scopes requires a separate install flow.

steps.title: Generate an install URL
steps.detail: Construct https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&scope=BOT_SCOPES&user_scope=USER_SCOPES (if any). Use the state parameter if you need CSRF protection.

steps.title: Redirect the user to the install URL
steps.detail: Send the user to the URL; they will approve the scopes and be redirected back to your redirect URI with a code parameter.

steps.title: Exchange the code for an access token
steps.detail: POST to https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access with client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri. Store the returned access_token (and optional refresh_token).

steps.title: Persist tokens per workspace
steps.detail: If the app will be installed in multiple workspaces, save each workspace’s tokens (and associated team ID) in a database.

approval_claim.text: The app was created and installed to my own workspace with no review. The only review path shown is the Marketplace 'Prepare & Submit' section in the sidebar, with five steps: Your App Listing, Review scopes, Security and compliance, Testing information, Automated checks. It is optional.

unreviewed_limits.text: The wizard installed the app into the developer's own workspace immediately, with the chosen bot scope (chat:write) active. Installing into other workspaces was not tested.

review_artifacts.text: If you submit to the Slack App Directory, you may need a privacy policy URL and scope justification, but this is not detailed in the provided docs.

approval_wait.note: Docs do not mention review timing.

setup_time.note: Measured once on 2026-10-22. Needs a Slack workspace you belong to (created a free one first, ~2 min). api.slack.com/apps → 'Create new app' is now a 4-step wizard: choose a start (templates 'AI agent' / 'Starter app', 'From a manifest', 'Blank app', or the Slack CLI), name + workspace, pick scopes, finish. On finishing, the dialog says the app 'was created and installed to the selected workspace' and shows the credentials in a collapsible 'Your app credentials' panel. No review, no wait.

redirect_uri_rules.text: OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs. http://localhost:8000/callback was accepted and saved (no HTTPS requirement for localhost). The page states that a URL passed in an OAuth request 'must (partially) match' one of the saved URLs, so matching is prefix-based, not exact. Redirect URLs are only needed to generate the 'Add to Slack' button or to distribute the app.

token_lifecycle.text: Docs do not describe token expiration or refresh mechanics; OAuth v2 returns an access_token (and optionally a refresh_token).

scopes_note.text: Bot scopes are passed via scope= parameter; user scopes via user_scope=. Each distinct set of scopes requires a separate install flow.

pkce_required.text: PKCE is not mentioned in the OAuth flow documentation; Slack’s OAuth v2 does not require it.

blockers.fix: Ensure the exact HTTPS URL used in the install flow is listed in the app’s OAuth & Permissions page.
Add all needed bot and/or user scopes before generating the install URL; each new scope set needs a new install flow.
Use v2 endpoints (https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize) for modern apps; classic apps require v1 endpoints and authVersion='v1' in SDK.
Provide a stateSecret to the InstallProvider and include a state parameter in the install URL to protect against CSRF.
Use the @slack/web-api Sign‑in With Slack docs instead; the @slack/oauth package does not support it.

blockers.blocker: The 'From scratch' option that older docs and tutorials describe no longer exists; the create dialog offers templates, a manifest upload, 'Blank app', or the Slack CLI.
blockers.fix: Choose 'Blank app' for the equivalent of the old 'From scratch' flow.

blockers.blocker: Scopes are chosen inside the creation wizard; an app created with no scopes has nothing to request at install time.
blockers.fix: Add at least one bot scope (e.g. chat:write) in the wizard, or later under OAuth & Permissions → Scopes.

agent_can: build the Slack install URL with client_id, scopes, and optional state
parse the OAuth callback to extract the authorization code
exchange the code for an access token via Slack’s token endpoint
store and retrieve tokens per workspace
human_must: create the Slack app in the developer portal
approve the install flow in the Slack UI
handle the server‑side token exchange (if not automated)
manage any marketplace submission or compliance documentation
composio_note: Composio has a 'slack' toolkit (https://docs.composio.dev/kb/toolkit/slack). Composio's own OAuth credential guide for it: https://composio.dev/auth/slack. When registering, use the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config.

whether any review is required for non‑marketplace apps

tested_notes.text: Scopes page shows a 'Required' toggle per scope and says changes in optional status apply immediately to a published app 'as long as the scopes are already approved' — scope approval is part of the Marketplace review, not of creating the app.
Credentials (Client ID / Client Secret / Signing Secret) are under Basic Information → App Credentials and were also shown on the wizard's final screen.
Corrects the generated guide's uncertainty: the gate is 'marketplace_only', not 'unknown'; private/own-workspace use needs no review at all.
The Slack CLI (`slack create`, `slack run`) is offered as an alternative to the web form, so most of the setup could be done by an agent from a terminal, except logging in.

difficulty.label: Easy
reasons: Review only if you list on the marketplace
